image_description: A white spoonbill wading in shallow, rippled water. The bird is captured in profile facing right, displaying its characteristic long, black, spatulate bill and predominantly white plumage. One dark leg is visible supporting the bird, while the other is obscured by the body or water. The background consists of out-of-focus greyish water.

The visible leg seems to merge into the water without a clear foot structure or distinct splash/displacement line. It looks like a stick ending in the water rather than a foot submerged.

Verify if the bill's spatulate shape is geometrically accurate or if it warps near the tip.
